name: Epidemiology and outbreak investigation
description: Outbreak investigation, surveillance and response for exercises: the terms and sequence field epidemiologists use, the products they issue (case reports, questionnaires, exposure notices, clinician alerts, letters, guidance), the decisions they make and the clocks they are measured on. Includes epidemic curves, line lists, attack-rate tables, contact networks, laboratory and dispensing boards, wastewater series, and simulated outbreaks. Stays at public health response decisions; it carries no pathogen handling detail.
outsideParties: school districts and child care centers

advisorRoles.name: Infection preventionist adviser

advisorRoles.name: Public health laboratory adviser

glossary.definition: Person, place, time and clinical or lab criteria for counting a case; tiers confirmed, probable, suspect. Broad early, tightened later.
Cases by onset time. Point source: one peak within one incubation period. Continuous source: plateau. Person to person: peaks one incubation apart.
Onset minus the longest and shortest incubation period; for a place, the case's presence inside the infectious period.
Attack rate = ill / exposed. The likely vehicle has the highest rate among those exposed and a high odds ratio (cases exposed x controls unexposed / cases unexposed x controls exposed).
Isolation: ill or infectious people. Quarantine: exposed people who are not ill.
Prepare; confirm diagnosis; confirm outbreak; count cases; describe by time, place, person; consider control now; test hypotheses; plan studies; control and evaluate; communicate.
Incubation 12 to 48 h; contagious until 2 days after symptoms stop; food workers excluded 48 h after (CDC, FDA Food Code).
Incubation 6 h to 6 d, usually 12 to 72 h; illness 4 to 7 d (CDC).
Incubation 7 to 21 d to rash (about 14); infectious 4 d before to 4 d after rash; airborne up to 2 h; MMR within 72 h or IG within 6 d; exclude susceptible contacts day 5 to 21 (CDC).
Incubation 1 to 4 d; infectious about 1 d before to 5 to 7 d after onset (CDC).
Incubation about 2 to 14 d, shorter in recent variants; guidance changes, use the current local rule and date it (CDC).
Incubation 7 to 10 d (5 to 21); infectious to 3 weeks after cough onset, or 5 d of antibiotics (CDC).
Incubation 2 to 14 d (to 19); not person to person; source is a building water system (CDC).

productConventions: Counts name the tier and time: 'N confirmed, N probable as of 14:00'.
Curves use onset date (hour for a point source); mark exposure and interventions.
Exposure notice: each place, address, date and exact time window; who acts; symptoms; watch-until date.
Clinician alert: Health Alert, Health Advisory or Health Update; number, date, case definition, numbered actions, how to report.
Isolation or quarantine sheet: exact first and last day and how the dates were set.
Line lists, rosters and exports: fictional people by code; marked exercise material.
realismRules: Never order a curve by report date.
Counts in notices, releases and letters match the line list at the stated time.
Show exposure-window arithmetic in controller notes.
Name a food vehicle only after the attack-rate table supports it.
Some contacts are unreachable; report them.
The health department recommends; the health officer orders.
Never give pathogen culture, growth, enhancement or handling detail.
Simulated series are never presented as historical.

criticalTasks: Confirm the diagnosis and decide, on a stated basis, whether cases exceed what is expected.
Adopt a case definition with confirmed, probable and suspect tiers and revise it when facts change.
Count cases by onset time, place and person; keep the line list and the epidemic curve in agreement.
Test hypotheses with attack rates or odds ratios before naming a vehicle or source.
Recommend control measures before the investigation is complete; the health officer orders them.
Issue exposure notices with exact places and time windows computed from onset and the infectious period.
Identify, classify and reach contacts within the designer's target and report those who cannot be reached.
Set laboratory testing priorities and manage turnaround and referral.
Open and run dispensing sites at the planned throughput.
Keep one count of cases by tier that every message uses.
Track laboratory and reporting delays and state their effect on the numbers.
Update the line list and the curve on a stated cycle and date every figure.
Issue exposure notices, clinician alerts and letters that match the line list and the exposure window.
Give the public, clinicians, schools and employers the same advice at the same time.
Counter misinformation that names the wrong source or place.
Agree one case definition and one count among the health department, the hospital infection prevention team and the laboratory.
State who recommends and who orders each control measure.
Request CDC Epi-Aid when local and state capacity is not enough.

exerciseTags.label: PHEP Biological Incident 100 (discussion-based)
exerciseTags.description: Discuss potential public health roles, functions, and countermeasures when responding to a large-scale biological incident including pandemic influenza.
objectives: Public health roles and functions: equity considerations, and how public health coordinates with health care partners and regulatory agencies.
Jurisdictional risks and response capabilities for biological mass casualty incidents, and the jurisdiction's capability to assess the health needs of affected populations and protect responders.
Medical countermeasures: strategies to distribute and dispense or administer them efficiently and to measure throughput.
Laboratory: the role of the Laboratory Response Network for Biological Threats (LRN-B) in a large-scale biological incident response.
exerciseTags.participants: Public health, emergency management, public health biological laboratories, environmental health programs, health care coalitions, and other partners responsible for coordinating or supporting response and recovery to a mass casualty biological incident.
exerciseTags.frequency: Once during the period of performance
capabilities: Capability 8: Medical Countermeasure Dispensing and Administration
Capability 9: Medical Materiel Management and Distribution
notes: Administrative preparedness and rural, frontier and tribal coordination discussion exercises cannot be used to fulfill it.

exerciseTags.label: PHEP Biological Incident 200 (functional exercise)
exerciseTags.description: Validate and evaluate the various aspects of a public health response to a biological incident: dispensing, administration, throughput, distribution, partnerships, and biological laboratory participation.
objectives: Capability 8: determine MCM dispensing and administration strategies; receive MCMs; activate dispensing or administration operations; dispense or administer MCMs to targeted populations.
Capability 9: acquire medical materiel from national stockpiles or other sources; distribute it; monitor inventories and distribution operations; recover materiel and demobilize.
exerciseTags.participants: Public health, emergency management, public health biological laboratories, environmental health programs, health care coalitions, and other partners responsible for coordinating or supporting response and recovery to a mass casualty biological incident.
exerciseTags.frequency: Once during the period of performance
capabilities: Capability 8: Medical Countermeasure Dispensing and Administration
Capability 9: Medical Materiel Management and Distribution
notes: CRI-funded jurisdictions must include staff notification and assembly of site core management teams, activation of the selected dispensing or vaccination site, set up of at least one site (open or closed), and dispensing, administering and tracking MCM inventories.
Seasonal influenza clinics cannot be used to fulfill the Biological Incident track.
It cannot replace Capstone 300 when a biological threat is the capstone risk.

exerciseTags.label: PHEP Capstone 100 (discussion-based)
exerciseTags.description: Discuss aspects of preparing and conducting the capstone full-scale exercise for the jurisdictional priority risk. A prior chemical, biological, radiological or nuclear, or natural disaster discussion exercise can meet it when aligned to the risk assessment.
objectives: Public health roles and functions for the chosen risk, including equity considerations and coordination with health care partners and regulatory agencies.
Jurisdictional risks and response capabilities for the chosen risk.
Medical countermeasure and medical materiel management strategies, with throughput and inventories measured.
exerciseTags.participants: Public health, emergency management, and other partners responsible for coordinating or supporting response and recovery efforts for the jurisdictional risk chosen as the primary focus of the capstone exercise.
exerciseTags.frequency: Once during the period of performance
capabilities: Capability 8: Medical Countermeasure Dispensing and Administration
Capability 9: Medical Materiel Management and Distribution

exerciseTags.label: PHEP Capstone 200 (drill)
exerciseTags.description: Exercise one specific primary operation or function critical to the success of the capstone exercise.
objectives: Test and validate at least one critical response function based on the jurisdictional risk chosen for the capstone.
exerciseTags.participants: Public health, emergency management, and other partners responsible for coordinating or supporting response and recovery efforts for the jurisdictional risk chosen as the primary focus of the capstone exercise.
exerciseTags.frequency: Once during the period of performance

exerciseTags.label: PHEP Capstone 300 (functional exercise)
exerciseTags.description: Validate and evaluate multiple response capabilities critical to the success of the capstone exercise.
objectives: Incorporate the applicable public health capability functions related to the risk identified in the risk assessment.
Include the five cross-cutting program priorities: partnerships, health equity, risk communications, data modernization and recovery.
exerciseTags.participants: Public health, emergency management, and other partners responsible for coordinating or supporting response and recovery efforts for the jurisdictional risk chosen as the primary focus of the capstone exercise.
exerciseTags.frequency: Once during the period of performance
notes: If a biological threat is the capstone risk, it must focus on the areas for improvement from the Biological Incident 200 exercise.

exerciseTags.label: PHEP Capstone 400 (full-scale exercise)
exerciseTags.description: Test the ability of the jurisdiction to operationalize response plans for the risk selected in the risk assessment.
objectives: Incorporate the applicable public health capability functions related to the risk identified in the risk assessment.
Include the five cross-cutting program priorities: partnerships, health equity, risk communications, data modernization and recovery.
exerciseTags.participants: Public health, emergency management, and other partners responsible for coordinating or supporting response and recovery efforts for the jurisdictional risk chosen as the primary focus of the capstone exercise.
exerciseTags.frequency: Once during the period of performance

exerciseTags.label: PHEP Critical Contacts Drill
exerciseTags.description: Test and validate critical contact information for the on-call epidemiologist, laboratorian and PHEP director; optionally exercise internal notification systems.
objectives: Contact: ensure on-call staff have access to on-call contact numbers and that the numbers work.
Verify: verify and update on-call critical contact numbers.
Optional: exercise additional internal notification procedures.
exerciseTags.participants: On-call epidemiologist, on-call LRN-B or LRN-C personnel, and the on-call PHEP director.
capabilities: Capability 13: Public Health Surveillance and Epidemiological Investigation
notes: Unannounced, conducted Monday to Friday, and alternating each year between biological and chemical laboratory on-call staff.
Performance target: 60 minutes from the CDC Emergency Operations Center contacting the on-call epidemiologist to the PHEP director and the LRN contacts notifying the EOC watch officer.
